note: General descriptions of relief that may be available. Eligibility is individual and fact-specific. This is not legal advice.

paths.name: Asylum
paths.constraint: Requires persecution or a well-founded fear of persecution on a protected ground, and must normally be filed within one year of arrival.
paths.detail: The one-year deadline has a written exception that matters here. 8 CFR 208.4(a)(5)(iv) lists as an extraordinary circumstance excusing a late filing that the applicant "maintained Temporary Protected Status, lawful immigrant or nonimmigrant status, or was given parole, until a reasonable period before the filing of the asylum application." Someone who held TPS for years and is now losing it is therefore not automatically time-barred, provided they file within a reasonable period.

paths.name: Family-based petition
paths.constraint: A U.S. citizen may petition a spouse, child, parent or sibling; a permanent resident may petition only a spouse or unmarried son or daughter.
paths.detail: Immediate relatives of U.S. citizens are not numerically capped. The F1 through F4 preference categories are capped and backlogged — see the wait-times section.

paths.name: Employment-based petition
paths.constraint: About 140,000 visas a year across five preference categories; most require Department of Labor certification and an employer-filed I-140.
paths.detail: EB-1 extraordinary ability and the EB-2 national interest waiver allow a person to petition for themselves without an employer.

paths.name: U visa
paths.constraint: For victims of qualifying criminal activity who suffered substantial physical or mental abuse and are helpful to law enforcement.
paths.detail: Requires a law-enforcement certification on Form I-918 Supplement B.

source.org: USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 3 Pt. C Ch. 2

paths.name: T visa
paths.constraint: For victims of a severe form of human trafficking who are present on account of that trafficking.
paths.detail: Force, fraud or coercion is not required for minors in commercial sex. There is no filing deadline.

source.org: USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 3 Pt. B Ch. 2

paths.name: VAWA self-petition
paths.constraint: For a person subjected to battery or extreme cruelty by a U.S. citizen or permanent resident spouse, parent, or adult son or daughter.
paths.detail: Filed on Form I-360 without the abuser's knowledge or consent. VAWA self-petitioners are exempt from the INA 245(a) entry requirement.

source.org: USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 3 Pt. D Ch. 2

paths.name: Adjustment of status under INA 245(a)
paths.constraint: Requires having been "inspected and admitted or paroled," being physically present, and having an immigrant visa immediately available.
paths.detail: TPS clears a different hurdle — USCIS treats TPS holders as being in lawful status for INA 245(c)(2) purposes — but it does not by itself supply the qualifying entry. Someone who entered without inspection and later received TPS still lacks one. See the travel-authorization note below.

source.org: USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 7 Pt. B Ch. 2

paths.name: Travel authorization and the 245(a) entry problem
paths.constraint: A TPS holder who travelled abroad on Form I-512T and was admitted on return may have cured the entry defect.
paths.detail: Effective July 1, 2022 USCIS rescinded Matter of Z-R-Z-C- and replaced Form I-512L with Form I-512T, which permits CBP to admit the bearer into TPS. Current policy states that TPS beneficiaries whom DHS has inspected and admitted into TPS after such authorized travel are "inspected and admitted" for purposes of adjustment. For a person who originally entered without inspection, this is often the single fact that decides whether a green-card case is possible.

source.org: USCIS Policy Alert, TPS and Adjustment of Status

paths.name: Voluntary departure
paths.constraint: Leaving without a removal order, which preserves some future eligibility.
paths.detail: Pre-conclusion voluntary departure allows up to 120 days but requires conceding removability and waiving other relief. At the conclusion of proceedings it allows up to 60 days, requires one year of prior physical presence, and requires posting a bond of at least $500 within five business days.
